title: Residential Property Condition Disclosure Statement
description: Oklahoma requires sellers of residential real property to provide a written Residential Property Condition Disclosure Statement to the buyer. The statement covers structural components, mechanical systems, environmental hazards, roof, foundation, plumbing, electrical, and other known material conditions. Must be delivered before or at the time of contract execution.

required_actions.note: Exemptions include foreclosure sales, transfers by fiduciary, new construction, and transfers between co-owners.

title: Brokerage Relationship Disclosure
description: Oklahoma brokers must disclose their agency relationship to all parties at the initiation of brokerage services. Oklahoma recognizes single-party brokerage, transaction brokerage, and dual agency. Dual agency requires written informed consent from all parties. The broker must provide the statutory disclosure form.

title: Closing Type — Title Company / Abstract
description: Oklahoma residential closings are typically handled by title companies or closing/abstract companies. Attorney involvement is not required by statute. Oklahoma uses both title insurance and abstract-and-attorney-opinion methods for verifying title. The abstract system is still common in rural areas.

required_actions.note: Title company or abstract company conducts closing. Attorney opinion may be used in lieu of title insurance in some areas.

title: Earthquake Activity Awareness
description: Oklahoma has experienced a significant increase in seismic activity since 2009, largely attributed to wastewater injection wells from oil and gas operations. While there is no specific statutory mandate for earthquake disclosure, prudent practice requires sellers to disclose known earthquake damage. The Oklahoma Corporation Commission monitors seismic activity and has implemented well shut-in protocols.

required_actions.note: Disclose any known earthquake damage on OK-RPCDS. Reference Oklahoma Geological Survey seismicity maps.

citations: Oklahoma Corporation Commission Order No. 636155 (seismicity response)

title: Lead-Based Paint Disclosure (Pre-1978)
description: For residential properties built before 1978, sellers must comply with the federal lead-based paint disclosure requirements. Oklahoma enforces the federal mandate requiring disclosure of known lead-based paint, provision of the EPA pamphlet, and a 10-day inspection opportunity.

required_actions.note: Buyer has 10-day inspection opportunity unless waived in writing.
